claims.text: This module produces NO partition and serves no UI. It produces MEASUREMENTS ABOUT A PARTITION WE ALREADY DECLARED
claims.why: The claim about producing no partition and no UI cannot be verified from this chunk alone; the rest of the file may contain code that contradicts it.

claims.text: Both call networkx/scipy. If you are adding a fifth spectral thing, extend one of these two rather than opening a third.
claims.why: This chunk imports networkx but does not show the other module (structcore.topology). The claim about both calling networkx/scipy cannot be fully checked.

claims.text: There is exactly one import-graph extractor on the mapping side and it is reach.analyse. graph_from_reach is an adapter over its output, not a second walker.
claims.why: The claim about reach.analyse being the only extractor cannot be verified from this chunk; no other mapping modules are shown.

claims.text: Nothing here returns an exit code, blocks a lane, moves a picker band, or decides anything.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the full file; later code might include such behavior.

claims.text: There is no threshold constant in this file on purpose.
claims.why: No threshold constants are defined in this chunk; only DEFAULT_TRIALS, DEFAULT_SEED, DEFAULT_K_MAX are present, which are not thresholds for blocking decisions.

claims.text: Undirected on purpose: Laplacian spectral theory as used here (Fiedler vector, algebraic connectivity, modularity, conductance) is defined for undirected graphs.
claims.why: The functions graph_from_edges and graph_from_reach both create undirected nx.Graph objects, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: graph_from_edges: Exists so a synthetic graph with known ground truth can be measured by the exact code path the repo graph goes through.
claims.why: The function is defined and exported; it creates an undirected graph from a mapping, suitable for synthetic inputs.

claims.text: graph_from_reach: It exists because the whole-repo reading is dominated by a partition artifact: tests/ is ~half the modules, and test files import the code under test and never each other, so the test package scores leak_rate 1.0 with zero internal edges.
claims.why: The claim about leak_rate and test package behavior refers to concepts not present in this chunk.

claims.text: graph_from_reach: Pass scope_prefixes=("daedalus/",) to measure the shipped package's own structure. Report which one you took; the two are not comparable.
claims.why: The claim about comparability cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: declared_partition: This is the partition the metrics below judge. It is read off the tree, not proposed by any algorithm -- the whole point is to score a human decision.
claims.why: The function groups modules by declared_package(module), which is imported from inventory, not an algorithm. The claim is consistent with the code.

claims.text: _communities: Partition as a list of node sets covering exactly graph's nodes.
claims.why: The function iterates over partition values, adds nodes present in graph, and adds any missing graph nodes as a final block. This covers exactly the graph's nodes.

claims.text: _giant: The largest connected component, as a subgraph view copy.
claims.why: The function computes connected components, picks the largest, and returns graph.subgraph(biggest).copy().

claims.text: fiedler_report: Reported on the largest connected component when the graph is disconnected: a disconnected graph has algebraic connectivity exactly 0 and no unique Fiedler vector, and fabricating one would be the numerology this module exists to prevent. Both the global 0.0 and the component value are returned, labelled, so neither can be quoted as the other.
claims.why: The function implementation is truncated in this chunk; the return dict for the disconnected case is not fully shown. The claim about returning both global 0.0 and component value cannot be verified.
